title: Optimize quant kernels: INT8/FP8 smoothquant + dequant fusion + KV-cache/batching scheduler
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: reduce per-token cost and tail latency for quantized models by improving fused kernels and scheduling when KV-cache and continuous batching are active. This PR targets INT8 and FP8 execution paths and folds SmoothQuant scaling and dequant operations into the main GEMM/attention kernels to avoid extra memory traffic and kernel launches. It also includes scheduler heuristics to prioritize hot KV-cache hits and reduce batching stalls for short-context chats.

Summary of changes: folded SmoothQuant rescaling into weight pretransform path for INT8/FP8 models; implemented dequantization-on-the-fly inside attention and FFN kernels to avoid separate dequant buffers; added a fused kernel variant (q_attn_fused_dequant) that consumes quantized KV directly; updated KV-cache eviction/warmup policy so hot entries avoid full re-quantization; introduced a small scheduling change that fast-paths single-step, low-seq-length requests to keep latency SLOs while preserving throughput for batched workloads.

Benchmarks: microbenchmarks on A100-80GB and H100 show 1.25x-1.7x throughput improvement and 8-25% p95 latency reduction for representative chat workloads with INT8/FP8 quantized Llama-like models. See perf/benchmarks/quant-kernels/experiment-2026-02-20 for raw numbers (summaries included below).

Testing: unit tests for fused kernels, stress tests for KV cache warmup, and end-to-end smoke tests for streaming/chat were added. Perf CI includes synthetic workload runs and a small end-to-end check against a baseline.

Checklist:
- [x] Fold SmoothQuant scaling into pretransform path
- [x] Implement fused dequant-attention and fused dequant-ffn kernels
- [x] Update scheduler to reduce batching stalls
- [x] Add KV-cache hot entry policy to avoid re-quantization
- [x] Add unit and perf tests
- [x] Update docs and release notes

Related: ENG-1624 (quant-kernel roadmap), ENG-1702 (kvcache scheduling improvements).

review_comments: Diego Martinez: Can you add a short note about correctness guarantees when folding SmoothQuant scaling? I want to ensure we don't change numerical behavior for FP32 fallback paths.

Asha Patel: Reply: folding is limited to quantized weight pretransform and guarded by a model-compat flag. FP32 code paths untouched. Added comments and a unit test that compares pre/post transform outputs within tolerance.
Ravi Singh: The scheduler change looks reasonable but please add a guard to disable the fast-path if perf CI shows regression on long-sequence workloads.
Asha Patel: Reply: added a feature-flag and a simple perf gate that disables the fast-path when microbenchmarks detect >1.03x regression on long sequences. Documented in continuous_batcher.cc.
Elena Kuznetsova: Tests look good. One nit: prefer smaller kernel launch grid for short sequences to reduce SM occupancy churn.
Asha Patel: Reply: adjusted launch configs and added heuristics in launch_config.h per Elena's suggestion. Re-ran perf CI.
Diego Martinez: Approving after CI green. Great work on reducing memory churn in the quant path.
merge_details: Merged by Diego Martinez (squash and merge). Commit message summarised PR changes and included a link to perf bench results and ENG tickets.
release_notes: Performance: Improved INT8/FP8 quantized kernel throughput (1.25x-1.7x) and reduced p95 latency (8-25%) for quantized chat workloads by fusing SmoothQuant scaling and dequant paths into attention/FFN kernels; improved KV-cache warmup and scheduler fast-paths to reduce batching stalls. No breaking API changes.
risk_assessment: Medium: changes are confined to quantized runtime paths behind model-compat feature flags. Unit and stress tests added. There's a small risk of regressions on obscure model shapes; perf gate disables scheduler fast-path on regression. Will monitor perf dashboards and rollout to Dedicated with canary first.
